newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares surge on wave of EMU optimism.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares surge on wave of EMU optimism.

text.p: Italian shares closed sharply higher on Thursday on a surge of buying prompted by hopes that France and its EU partners can agree on a stability pact, a strong showing on Wall Street and underlying buoyancy in the bond market.

The all-share Mibtel index finished 2.09 percent higher at 12,469 with the blue chip Mib30 jumping 2.7 percent to 18,807. Trading volume leaped 1.632 trillion lire, well up from 923.459 billion on Wednesday.
A call by Bank of Italy Governor Antonio Fazio for government spending cuts failed to unsettle a market which appears no longer to be discounting an imminent discount rate cut, traders said.
One trader said he was puzzled at the sudden mood swing in the market and was unsure how long the positive trend could last.

Among banks, Credito Italiano rocketed 8.61 percent to 2,862 lire, boosted by an upgrade from Goldman Sachs. The U.S. investment bank raised Credito to its European priority list from a market outperformer.
Parmalat had another good day, making up the ground that it lost after launching a bid for Canadian food producer Ault, closing 6.4 percent higher at 2,512 lire.

Telecom ordinary shares all advanced but STET and Telecom Italia savings stocks retreated further after their dive at the beginning of the week following the Treasury's announcement that it would not allow their conversion into ordinary shares.
ENI and Fiat were relatively subdued rising 1.35 percent to 9.030 lire and 0.98 percent to 5,856 lire, respectively.
